newsitem.title: USA: Stevens sees Q4 loss, revises credit terms.
newsitem.headline: Stevens sees Q4 loss, revises credit terms.

text.p: Stevens International Inc said on Tuesday it expects to report a "significant" fourth-quarter loss for 1996, which will exceed the $4.1 million net loss it incurred in the third quarter.

Stevens also said it revised its agreement with its senior lender, Bank of America Texas NA, into a bridge arrangement to provide a revolving line of credit at higher interest rates until Stevens sells its Bernal division on February 28.

The company has signed a letter of intent to sell the division to a Michigan-based investment group that includes former Bernal owners. After the sale is completed, Stevens intends to negotiate a longer-term credit facility. Meanwhile, it did not make its year-end interest payment to subordinated debt holders.
Stevens also is cutting 154 jobs by closing a plant in Hamilton, Ohio, as part of an expanded restructuring program.
"We have a revised operating plan that calls for significant cost cuts, streamlined operations and improved productivity," Chairman Paul I. Stevens said in a statement released by the company.
